explanation: A thickened mordant paste confines alum to printed areas, so colour develops only there.
conditions: Inference: rheology evidence is from modern screen printing and the thickener of Indian alum paste is not documented here.
removal_reason: Self-described inference; rheology evidence is from screen printing, the Indian alum-paste thickener is undocumented.

explanation: The mechanism (clay survives only short, cold immersions) matches the Sanganeri dyer's practice of opening pleats gently and keeping the alum dip to a few minutes so the dabu does not crack or come off.
conditions: The Dabu mechanism comes from a workshop source (Pratt) and is needs_evidence in its file; the link is an inference across files.
removal_reason: Inference across files; no source compares these.

explanation: As above for Bagru: gentle unfolding avoids cracking the dabu, and a long alum dip makes the dabu come off.
conditions: Inference across files; Dabu mechanism is needs_evidence.
removal_reason: Inference across files; no source compares these.

explanation: The vichharnu stage uses this tool.
conditions: The GI text names washing tanks only for the resist-washing stage; their use in the final wash is inferred.
removal_reason: Self-described inference: the GI names washing tanks only for resist washing.

explanation: Harara (tannin source) plus iron mordant parallels iron–tannin black; Bagh sources describe the black as iron + alizarin.
conditions: Bagh sources do not explicitly invoke iron–tannin chemistry.
removal_reason: Self-described: Bagh sources do not invoke iron-tannin chemistry.

explanation: Fine-line small motifs require finely carved small hardwood blocks.
conditions: Inferred: sources describe small, finely carved blocks and fine-line motifs but do not state the requirement explicitly.
removal_reason: Self-described inference; requirement not stated by sources.

explanation: Ageing lets mordant paste penetrate the fibre; the GI also specifies a print visible on the underside.
conditions: Link inferred from the two GI statements; not stated as causal in sources.
removal_reason: Self-described inference; causal link not stated by sources.

explanation: Repetitive trade designs favoured blocks.
removal_reason: No source attributes the pen-to-block shift to the trade; sources only record that blocks later took over.

explanation: The khariyanu stage uses this tool.
removal_reason: DR-120 source check: S1 p. 5 describes the tari only as a printing tray layered by the kind of printing; no recorded source names it for khariyanu.

explanation: The pa stage uses this tool.
removal_reason: DR-120 source check: S1 p. 5 describes the tari only as a printing tray layered by the kind of printing; no recorded source names it for pa.

explanation: Iron in water darkens tannin-treated cloth (black spots), the same reaction exploited in kut.
removal_reason: DR-120 source check: S10 reports black spots from iron in water but names no tannin; S1 states the iron-tannic reaction only for kut. No recorded source states the link.

explanation: Harara treatment before printing is a myrobalan (tannin) pre-treatment reported to brighten red and black.
conditions: Bagh sources report the brightening effect of harara but do not name tannin or mordanting chemistry.
removal_reason: Bagh content verification 2026-11-07 (DR-120): neither cited source (GI Journal 75, Jain 2019) names tannin or a mordanting effect of harara; they report only the brighter red and black.

explanation: Double-dye effects involve sequential or combined processing of colours.
conditions: The GI text describes double dye and optional over-dyeing separately; it does not say double dye is done through the over-dyeing stage.
removal_reason: Bagh content verification 2026-11-07 (DR-120): GI Journal 75 describes the double dye and the optional over-dyeing separately and never says the double dye is done through the over-dyeing stage.

explanation: Washing generates effluent (GI dossier: aerated before discharge); Gaatha reports chemicals in the water seeping underground. No source directly measures final-washing effluent as the cause.
removal_reason: No recorded source ties groundwater pollution to the final washing: the GI dossier says only that effluent is aerated before discharge, and Gaatha attributes the pollution to chemicals in the process water in general (bagru-verification.md, DR-120).

explanation: Chhipa printers carry out the resist printing.
removal_reason: No recorded source has a Chippa practitioner explain resist printing: S1 (as told by a master craftsman) and S2 say only that Chippas print, so the link states more than its sources (DR-120).

explanation: Links the source's alkali-plus-heat account to the shared sun-bleaching mechanism.
removal_reason: DR-120 source check: S1 p. 11 explains tapai by alkali (cow dung) and the heat of the sun's rays; no recorded Sanganeri source states the shared light-oxidation mechanism.

explanation: Traditional scouring repeats wetting and drying on open ground over days.
removal_reason: DR-120 source check: S1 p. 10 describes scouring as wetting and drying on open ground for 3 to 6 days; no recorded source ties it to sun or climate.

explanation: Dried harda cloth is beaten with a wooden mallet.
removal_reason: DR-120 source check: S1 p. 10 beats the dried harda cloth with 'a wooden mallet'; S1 p. 13 defines the mogri as a mallet for the folds of moist finished cloth, and no recorded source names the harda mallet as the mogri. The mogri stays linked to the tradition through the GI tool list.

explanation: Coromandel soil, water and dye plants is documented as part of Machilipatnam block-printed kalamkari.
removal_reason: DR-120 source check: S11 ties the favourable soil, water and dye plants to the Coromandel Coast and never names Machilipatnam, Masulipatnam or Pedana; no recorded source ties them to this tradition.

explanation: Sequential order of production stages as documented.
removal_reason: DR-120 source check: S4 p. 4 lists block making first among the stages, but the list is not in time order (bleaching and washing is item 7), and no recorded source orders block making before the cloth is scoured.

explanation: Final finished cloth.
removal_reason: DR-120 source check: S4 p. 12 credits the fixing of all colours to the alum dip and p. 13 calls soaping the last stage; S3 has no fastness statement; no recorded source says the soap wash produces colourfast cloth.

explanation: Indigo fixes by its own (vat) chemistry, not a mordant; vat process at Pedana not documented.
conditions: Pedana prints indigo paste directly; reduction details not sourced.
removal_reason: DR-120 source check: S10 says indigo needs no mordant and the cloth is immersed in the dye vat; no recorded source states vat reduction.

explanation: Cloth spread wet in sun as part of bleaching.
removal_reason: DR-120 source check: S4 and S5 list sun drying and bleaching as separate steps; no recorded source says the sun bleaches the cloth.

explanation: Resist blocks dye physically, whereas indigo colours by redox; resist is applied before the vat so covered areas stay undyed except along cracks.
removal_reason: DR-122 source check: S10 gives the mud resist and the indigo vat as successive steps of one process (the resist is printed on the areas to remain undyed, then the cloth goes into the vat); the only contrast it draws is mordant-dyed against resist-dyed. No recorded source contrasts the resist barrier with vat reduction.

explanation: Secondary sources give several GI years that differ from the registry record.
removal_reason: DR-124: no recorded source states the link; the juxtaposition was the curators' own and the Sanganeri side rested on sanganeri:S14 (unverified kind), as the round 2 source check of 2026-10-16 found.

explanation: The cloth is wetted and dried in the open, again and again, until it becomes white and bright.
conditions: Source describes the practice, not the mechanism.
removal_reason: Integration of DR-122 and DR-124: S1 p. 9 describes scouring as sprinkling and drying on large open grounds until the cloth is white; it names neither the sun nor bleaching, so no recorded Bagru source states the shared light-oxidation mechanism (as for Sanganeri scouring in DR-120).

explanation: Daboo is described as distinct from Bagru and Sanganeri prints in look and method.
removal_reason: Lead ruling 2026-11-08 (DR-131 follow-up): the only source, S19, is an unattributed Utsavpedia page; no attributed source among the 24 archived Dabu sources or a web search states that Dabu printing is distinct from both Bagru and Sanganeri prints, so the comparison and its link are removed rather than approved.
